# dlaqr2

> Performs the orthogonal similarity transformation of a Hessenberg matrix to detect and deflate fully converged eigenvalues from a trailing principal submatrix (aggressive early deflation).

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlaqr2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaqr2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlaqr2(
    order,
    wantt, wantz,
    N,
    ktop,
    kbot, nw,
    H, LDH,
    iloz, ihiz,
    Z, LDZ,
    ns,
    nd,
    SR, strideSR,
    SI, strideSI,
    V, LDV,
    nh,
    T, LDT,
    nv,
    WV, LDWV,
    WORK
) → Float64Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `wantt` | `boolean` | If `true`, then the Hessenberg matrix H is fully updated so that the quasi-triangular Schur factor may be computed (in cooperation with the calling subroutine). |
| `wantz` | `boolean` | If `true`, then the orthogonal matrix Z is updated so so that the orthogonal Schur factor may be computed (in cooperation with the calling subroutine). |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The order of the matrix H and (if WANTZ is `true`) the order of the orthogonal matrix Z. |
| `ktop` | `integer` | It is assumed that either KTOP = 1 or H(KTOP,KTOP-1)=0. |
| `kbot` | `NonNegativeInteger` | It is assumed without a check that either KBOT = N or H(KBOT+1,KBOT)=0. |
| `nw` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Deflation window size. 1 <= NW <= (KBOT-KTOP+1). |
| `H` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × N</sub> | **in/out** · On input the initial N-by-N section of H stores the Hessenberg matrix undergoing aggressive early deflation. |
| ↳ `LDH` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `H` |
| `iloz` | `integer` | Specify the rows of Z to which transformations must be applied if WANTZ is `true`. 1 <= ILOZ <= IHIZ <= N. |
| `ihiz` | `integer` | Specify the rows of Z to which transformations must be applied if WANTZ is `true`. 1 <= ILOZ <= IHIZ <= N. |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × N</sub> | **in/out** · IF WANTZ is `true`, then on output, the orthogonal similarity transformation mentioned above has been accumulated into Z(ILOZ:IHIZ,ILOZ:IHIZ) from the right. |
| ↳ `LDZ` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `Z` |
| `ns` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the number of unconverged (ie approximate) eigenvalues returned in SR and SI that may be used as shifts by the calling subroutine |
| `nd` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the number of converged eigenvalues uncovered by this subroutine |
| `SR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length kbot</sub> | **out** · On output, the real and imaginary parts of approximate eigenvalues that may be used for shifts are stored in SR(KBOT-ND-NS+1) through SR(KBOT-ND) and SI(KBOT-ND-NS+1) through SI(KBOT-ND), respectively. |
| ↳ `strideSR` | `integer` | Stride length for `SR` |
| `SI` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length kbot</sub> | **out** · On output, the real and imaginary parts of approximate eigenvalues that may be used for shifts are stored in SR(KBOT-ND-NS+1) through SR(KBOT-ND) and SI(KBOT-ND-NS+1) through SI(KBOT-ND), respectively. |
| ↳ `strideSI` | `integer` | Stride length for `SI` |
| `V` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × nw</sub> | **out** · An NW-by-NW work array. |
| ↳ `LDV` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `V` |
| `nh` | `integer` | The number of columns of T. |
| `T` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × nw</sub> | **out** · The leading dimension of T just as declared in the calling subroutine. |
| ↳ `LDT` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `T` |
| `nv` | `integer` | The number of rows of work array WV available for workspace. |
| `WV` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × nw</sub> | **out** · The leading dimension of W just as declared in the calling subroutine. |
| ↳ `LDWV` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `WV` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null` | **out** · Workspace of length at least `2*JW` (`JW = min(nw, kbot-ktop+1)`, the reference's `2*NW`), or `null` to allocate the reference's optimum (`JW + JW*32 + 4160` for `JW > 2`) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `wantt`: If .TRUE., then the Hessenberg matrix H is fully updated so that the quasi-triangular Schur factor may be computed (in cooperation with the calling subroutine). If .FALSE., then only enough of H is updated to preserve the eigenvalues.
- `wantz`: If .TRUE., then the orthogonal matrix Z is updated so so that the orthogonal Schur factor may be computed (in cooperation with the calling subroutine). If .FALSE., then Z is not referenced.
- `N`: The order of the matrix H and (if `WANTZ` is .TRUE.) the order of the orthogonal matrix Z.
- `ktop`: It is assumed that either `KTOP = 1` or $H(\mathrm{KTOP},\mathrm{KTOP}-1)=0$. `KBOT` and `KTOP` together determine an isolated block along the diagonal of the Hessenberg matrix.
- `kbot`: It is assumed without a check that either `KBOT = N` or $H(\mathrm{KBOT}+1,\mathrm{KBOT})=0$. `KBOT` and `KTOP` together determine an isolated block along the diagonal of the Hessenberg matrix.
- `nw`: Deflation window size. $1 \le \mathrm{NW} \le (\mathrm{KBOT}-\mathrm{KTOP}+1)$.
- `H`: On input the initial N-by-N section of H stores the Hessenberg matrix undergoing aggressive early deflation. On output H has been transformed by an orthogonal similarity transformation, perturbed, and the returned to Hessenberg form that (it is to be hoped) has some zero subdiagonal entries.
- `ihiz`: Specify the rows of Z to which transformations must be applied if `WANTZ` is .TRUE.. $1 \le \mathrm{ILOZ} \le \mathrm{IHIZ} \le N$.
- `Z`: IF `WANTZ` is .TRUE., then on output, the orthogonal similarity transformation mentioned above has been accumulated into `Z(ILOZ:IHIZ,ILOZ:IHIZ)` from the right. If `WANTZ` is .FALSE., then Z is unreferenced.
- `ns`: The number of unconverged (ie approximate) eigenvalues returned in `SR` and `SI` that may be used as shifts by the calling subroutine.
- `nd`: The number of converged eigenvalues uncovered by this subroutine.
- `SI`: On output, the real and imaginary parts of approximate eigenvalues that may be used for shifts are stored in `SR(KBOT-ND-NS+1)` through `SR(KBOT-ND)` and `SI(KBOT-ND-NS+1)` through `SI(KBOT-ND)`, respectively. The real and imaginary parts of converged eigenvalues are stored in `SR(KBOT-ND+1)` through `SR(KBOT)` and `SI(KBOT-ND+1)` through `SI(KBOT)`, respectively.
- `V`: An `NW`-by-`NW` work array.
- `nh`: The number of columns of T. $\mathrm{NH} \ge \mathrm{NW}$.
- `nv`: The number of rows of work array `WV` available for workspace. $\mathrm{NV} \ge \mathrm{NW}$.
- `WORK`: On exit, `WORK(1)` is set to an estimate of the optimal value of `LWORK` for the given values of N, `NW`, `KTOP` and `KBOT`.

</details>

**Returns** `Float64Array`: `WV`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` twenty-first argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nw )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` twenty-fourth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nw )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` twenty-seventh argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nw )` (row-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlaqr2.ndarray(
    wantt, wantz,
    N,
    ktop,
    kbot, nw,
    H, strideH1, strideH2, offsetH,
    iloz, ihiz,
    Z, strideZ1, strideZ2, offsetZ,
    ns,
    nd,
    SR, strideSR, offsetSR,
    SI, strideSI, offsetSI,
    V, strideV1, strideV2, offsetV,
    nh,
    T, strideT1, strideT2, offsetT,
    nv,
    WV, strideWV1, strideWV2, offsetWV,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → Float64Array
```

Performs aggressive early deflation on an upper Hessenberg matrix.

DLAQR2 is the non-recursive version. It always uses DLAHQR for the
eigenvalue computation of the deflation window.

Note: KTOP and KBOT are 1-based (Fortran convention).

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `wantt` | `boolean` | If true, fully update H for Schur form |
| `wantz` | `boolean` | If true, accumulate transformations in Z |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrix H |
| `ktop` | `integer` | Top of the active block (1-based) |
| `kbot` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Bottom of the active block (1-based) |
| `nw` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Deflation window size |
| `H` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × N</sub> | **in/out** · Upper Hessenberg matrix |
| ↳ `strideH1` | `integer` | Stride of first dim of H |
| ↳ `strideH2` | `integer` | Stride of second dim of H |
| ↳ `offsetH` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for H |
| `iloz` | `integer` | First row of Z to update (1-based) |
| `ihiz` | `integer` | Last row of Z to update (1-based) |
| `Z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × N</sub> | **in/out** · Orthogonal matrix |
| ↳ `strideZ1` | `integer` | Stride of first dim of Z |
| ↳ `strideZ2` | `integer` | Stride of second dim of Z |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for Z |
| `ns` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the number of unconverged (ie approximate) eigenvalues returned in SR and SI that may be used as shifts by the calling subroutine |
| `nd` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the number of converged eigenvalues uncovered by this subroutine |
| `SR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length kbot</sub> | **out** · Real parts of eigenvalues/shifts (output) |
| ↳ `strideSR` | `integer` | Stride for SR |
| ↳ `offsetSR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for SR |
| `SI` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length kbot</sub> | **out** · Imaginary parts of eigenvalues/shifts (output) |
| ↳ `strideSI` | `integer` | Stride for SI |
| ↳ `offsetSI` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for SI |
| `V` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × nw</sub> | **out** · NW-by-NW workspace matrix |
| ↳ `strideV1` | `integer` | Stride of first dim of V |
| ↳ `strideV2` | `integer` | Stride of second dim of V |
| ↳ `offsetV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for V |
| `nh` | `integer` | Number of columns available in T |
| `T` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × nw</sub> | **out** · NW-by-NH workspace matrix |
| ↳ `strideT1` | `integer` | Stride of first dim of T |
| ↳ `strideT2` | `integer` | Stride of second dim of T |
| ↳ `offsetT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for T |
| `nv` | `integer` | Number of rows available in WV |
| `WV` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>? × nw</sub> | **out** · NV-by-NW workspace matrix |
| ↳ `strideWV1` | `integer` | Stride of first dim of WV |
| ↳ `strideWV2` | `integer` | Stride of second dim of WV |
| ↳ `offsetWV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WV |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Workspace array; length at least `2*JW` (`JW = min(nw, kbot-ktop+1)`, the reference's `2*NW`); the reference's optimum (`JW + JW*32 + 4160` for `JW > 2`) keeps DGEHRD/DORMHR blocked |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `wantt`: If .TRUE., then the Hessenberg matrix H is fully updated so that the quasi-triangular Schur factor may be computed (in cooperation with the calling subroutine). If .FALSE., then only enough of H is updated to preserve the eigenvalues.
- `wantz`: If .TRUE., then the orthogonal matrix Z is updated so so that the orthogonal Schur factor may be computed (in cooperation with the calling subroutine). If .FALSE., then Z is not referenced.

- `ihiz`: Specify the rows of Z to which transformations must be applied if `WANTZ` is .TRUE.. $1 \le \mathrm{ILOZ} \le \mathrm{IHIZ} \le N$.
- `Z`: IF `WANTZ` is .TRUE., then on output, the orthogonal similarity transformation mentioned above has been accumulated into `Z(ILOZ:IHIZ,ILOZ:IHIZ)` from the right. If `WANTZ` is .FALSE., then Z is unreferenced.

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dlaqr2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaqr2';

/**
* Sets a column-major N-by-N matrix to the identity.
*
* @private
* @param {Float64Array} v - matrix elements (real view)
* @param {PositiveInteger} N - matrix order
* @param {PositiveInteger} k - number of real values per element
*/
function setIdentity( v, N, k ) {
	let i;
	for ( i = 0; i < N; i++ ) {
		v[ k * ( ( i * N ) + i ) ] = 1.0;
	}
}

const N = 6;
const NW = 3;
const ns = new Int32Array( 1 );
const nd = new Int32Array( 1 );

let H;
let Z;
let SR;
let SI;
let V;
let T;
let WV;
let WORK;

// 6-by-6 upper Hessenberg matrix (column-major); deflation window of NW rows:
H = new Float64Array( [ 4.6, 1.2, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.3, 1.5, -3.7, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, -3.4, -0.6, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.6, 3.8, 2.9, 0.20000000000000018, -1.5, 0.0, -2.6, 1.1, 0.4, -3.5, 3.4, -1.5, -0.4, 2.4, -2.0, 0.2, 1.8, 4.8 ] );
Z = new Float64Array( N * N );
setIdentity( Z, N, 1 );
SR = new Float64Array( N );
SI = new Float64Array( N );
V = new Float64Array( NW * NW );
T = new Float64Array( NW * NW );
WV = new Float64Array( N * NW );
WORK = new Float64Array( 2 * N * N );

// Using the standard interface:
dlaqr2( 'column-major', true, true, N, 1, N, NW, H, N, 1, N, Z, N, ns, nd, SR, 1, SI, 1, V, NW, NW, T, NW, N, WV, N, WORK );
console.log( 'ns = %d, nd = %d', ns[ 0 ], nd[ 0 ] );
console.log( SR );
console.log( SI );

// Using the ndarray interface:
H = new Float64Array( [ 4.6, 1.2, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.3, 1.5, -3.7, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, -3.4, -0.6, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.6, 3.8, 2.9, 0.20000000000000018, -1.5, 0.0, -2.6, 1.1, 0.4, -3.5, 3.4, -1.5, -0.4, 2.4, -2.0, 0.2, 1.8, 4.8 ] );
Z = new Float64Array( N * N );
setIdentity( Z, N, 1 );
SR = new Float64Array( N );
SI = new Float64Array( N );
V = new Float64Array( NW * NW );
T = new Float64Array( NW * NW );
WV = new Float64Array( N * NW );
WORK = new Float64Array( 2 * N * N );
dlaqr2.ndarray( true, true, N, 1, N, NW, H, 1, N, 0, 1, N, Z, 1, N, 0, ns, nd, SR, 1, 0, SI, 1, 0, V, 1, NW, 0, NW, T, 1, NW, 0, N, WV, 1, N, 0, WORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( 'ns = %d, nd = %d', ns[ 0 ], nd[ 0 ] );
console.log( SR );
console.log( SI );
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLAQR2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLAQR2 is identical to DLAQR3 except that it avoids recursion by calling DLAHQR instead of DLAQR4.

Aggressive early deflation:

This subroutine accepts as input an upper Hessenberg matrix H and performs an orthogonal similarity transformation designed to detect and deflate fully converged eigenvalues from a trailing principal submatrix. On output H has been over- written by a new Hessenberg matrix that is a perturbation of an orthogonal similarity transformation of H. It is to be hoped that the final version of H has many zero subdiagonal entries.

</section>
